item.title: A judge halted D.C. golf course renovations. Trump says they'll still start next month
item.description: A federal judge has barred the government from clearing more trees or making other alterations to D.C.'s East Potomac Park without proper notice. Trump says his administration will appeal.

item.title: Democrats have a midterm edge, poll shows. And, Israelis vote in high-stakes election
item.description: Democrats are still holding a slight edge with Election Day a week away, according to a new NPR/PBS News/Marist poll. And, Israelis are casting their votes in an election that could change leadership.

item.title: Can Black voting power and Trump fatigue break Mississippi's red wall?
item.description: Mississippi has the largest proportional Black population in the country. It's one reason the U.S. Senate race has seen millions in last-minute spending and high-profile campaign visits.

item.title: Polymarket has investigated 'dozens' of election-related cases
item.description: The prediction market has hired a former FBI official to make sure political insiders don't use the platform for profit from confidential election information.

item.title: Democrats still poised to make gains, but poll shows warning signs for just how many
item.description: Democrats hold significant advantages going into Election Day, according to a new NPR/PBS News/Marist poll. But lagging enthusiasm among key groups is just one indicator that gains may not come easy.

item.title: How congressional Democrats are preparing for claims of election fraud by Trump
item.description: Democrats in Congress are bracing for what they fear could be meddling by President Trump or his allies with the results of this year's midterm elections.

item.title: Data centers are a hot-button issue for Ohioans as midterms near
item.description: In Ohio, many people are displeased with the state's rapid buildout of data centers. It's a hot-button issue in the midterms, as political candidates from both parties try to ease voter concerns.

item.title: As campaign rhetoric escalates, Michigan voters say they're burned out
item.description: From college football tailgates to conversations in Ann Arbor, Michigan voters tell NPR they're worried about everyday costs, frustrated with the two-party system and increasingly reluctant to discuss politics openly.

item.title: Trump campaigns in Mississippi, highlighting Republicans' challenges
item.description: President Trump campaigned Monday in Mississippi, as he continued a closing midterm rally blitz that has highlighted Republicans' challenges ahead of an election that could drastically shift power in Washington.

item.title: Trump administration attempting to prosecute former FBI Director James Comey again
item.description: The Trump administration is attempting to prosecute James Comey for what it calls a decade-old leak of classified information. Comey's lawyers immediately dismissed the effort as invalid and outside the time limit.
